papers.title: Governed Hybrid Agency: A Critical Evidence Map of Cognitive Architectures for Foundation-Model Agents
papers.summary: Background. Cognitive architectures specify the persistent memories, representations, learning processes, and control loops that allow an artificial agent to remain coherent across tasks and time. Foundation models provide broad generative competence, but do not by themselves ensure grounded action, reliable long-horizon memory, calibrated uncertainty, execution monitoring, or accountable learning. Objectives. This critical integrative review examines how cognitive-architecture principles are being used to govern foundation-model agents. Taking the last comprehensive pre-foundation-model survey of cognitive architectures (Kotseruba & Tsotsos, first published online in 2018) as its historical baseline, it maps developments across twelve ability channels, identifies recurring integration patterns, and derives testable design and evaluation requirements. Methods. We combined a historical-theoretical synthesis with a focused, PRISMA-informed evidence map of English-language records indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection, searched in July 2026 over the 2018–2026 window. Queries required terms for cognitive architectures or architecture-level cognitive systems, foundation or generative models, and governance-relevant mechanisms. The searches identified 1,173 records; after deduplication, rule-based filtering, and LLMassisted title-and-abstract assessment, 119 works

papers.title: From Code Completion to Agentic Development: A Survey of AI Coding Agents, Ecosystems, and Evolving Software Engineering Practice
papers.summary: Abstract Large language models have extended software-development assistance from token-level completion to systems that can navigate repositories, edit files, execute tools, and iterate on test feedback. This survey studies the design, use, and evaluation of these AI coding agents, together with their commercial and societal context. Reproducible database queries support literature discovery, but the cited corpus is selected and coded for relevance; we therefore describe the work as a structured scoping survey rather than an exhaustive systematic review. We organize the field using five dimensions: interaction paradigm, computational architecture, deployment form, orchestration mode, and human-oversight mode. Treating oversight separately from architecture resolves a conceptual overlap in earlier classifications and gives each representative system one value per dimension. The technical synthesis covers repository context, planning, tool use, multi-agent coordination, SDLC applications, and benchmark limitations. We keep technical capability evidence separate from business and adoption reports. Vendor and news sources are used as dated context, not as proxies for maturity or user preference. The survey covers material available through 28 February 2026.

papers.title: AgentMesh: Toward Redundancy- and Barrier-Free Dataflow in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) now power long-running agentic applications like deep research and coding agents, yet their end-to-end latency reaches minutes to hours. The runtime executes each dataflow as an opaque, indivisible block at coarse granularity, wasting end-to-end time on redundancy (acquiring content already held or unnecessary) and barriers (a downstream component idling until its upstream input is entirely ready). We abstract a produce–transfer–consume dataflow as a basic unit in MAS, where the producer is a tool or LLM decoding, and the consumer is an LLM prefill. We present AgentMesh, a MAS runtime that optimizes each dataflow with three mechanisms: Delta Tool Retrieval (DTR) shrinks the produce step by serving a tool result’s cached items and fetching only the semantic delta; Branch-Parallel Prefill (BPP) shrinks the consume step by prefilling independent branches in parallel under dependency-graph-derived attention sparsity; Dynamic-Equilibrium Streaming (DES), a dynamic pipeline, overlaps produce, transfer, and consume by pacing streamed chunks to the runtime rate of producer and consumer. Implemented on AutoGen, OpenCode, and vLLM and evaluated across three GPU generations and six models, AgentMesh reduces end-to-end latency by up to 62% with no statistically significant quality loss, on both deep research and coding agent workloads.

papers.title: Comment and Control: Hijacking Agentic Workflows via Context-Grounded Evolution
papers.summary: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. While bringing convenience for developers, this integration exposes a new risk: An adversary may control and craft certain inputs, such as GitHub issue comments, to manipulate the LLM agent for unwanted actions, such as credential exfiltration and arbitrary command execution. To our knowledge, no prior academic work has studied such a risk in agentic workflows. In this paper, we design the first detection and exploitation framework, called JAW, to hijack agentic workflows hosted on automation platforms via a novel approach called Context-Grounded Evolution. Our key idea is to evolve agentic workflow inputs under the contexts derived from hybrid program analysis for hijacking purposes. Specifically, JAW generates agentic workflow contexts through three analyses: (i) static path-feasibility analysis to identify feasible agent-invocation paths and the input constraints required to trigger them, (ii) dynamic prompt-provenance analysis to determine how that input is transformed and embedded into the LLM context, and (iii) capability analysis to identify the actions and restrictions available to the agent at runtime. Our evaluation of JAW on GitHub workflows and n8n template

papers.title: 3CBench: a unified benchmarking framework for the computing capacity of heterogeneous AI clusters
papers.summary: Abstract The rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence has driven the demand for extensivecomputational resources and the deployment of AI tasks across heterogeneouscomputing platforms. However, existing benchmarking systems face several chal-lenges, including limited compatibility with diverse hardware, insufficient supportfor varied deep learning frameworks and tasks, and a lack of comprehensive eval-uation metrics for the computing capacities. To address these issues, we propose3CBench, a unified benchmarking framework designed for heterogeneous AI clus-ters. Featuring a modular architecture encompassing environment management,task execution, and metrics analysis, 3CBench provides automated workflows andensures seamless compatibility with diverse GPU architectures and deep learningframeworks. It provides a comprehensive evaluation metrics system to rigorouslyassess computational performance and stability across both transformer-basedlarge language models and convolutional neural networks, thereby covering dom-inant deep learning architectures. Extensive experiments demonstrate 3CBench’sscalability on heterogeneous AI clusters, compatibility with various deep learningframeworks and tasks, and the support for a wide range of applications. Addition-ally, 3CBench aids in problem diagnosis during the development process of GPUvendors. These features establish 3CBench as a robust

papers.title: The triadic convergence in Industry 5.0: Orchestrating resilient supply chains, agile project management, and algorithmic Islamic banking through smart contracts and green sukuk
papers.summary: Contemporary global value networks and capital-intensive infrastructure projects face an existential crisis driven by geopolitical disruptions, persistent inflation, and the fragile leverage of conventional interest-based debt. Although Supply Chain Management (SCM), Project Management (PM), and Islamic Banking (IB) have evolved rapidly in isolation, a unified framework integrating all three is absent. This article bridges that gap by formulating the Triadic Convergence Framework (TCF), a novel cyber-physical-financial architecture operating within the human-centric and sustainable ethos of Industry 5.0. Grounded in Transaction Cost Economics, Agency Theory, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and the socio-ethical axioms of Maqasid al-Shariah, this study employs a multi-layered conceptual and mathematical modeling approach. It synthesizes Q1 literature across artificial intelligence, blockchain-enabled Supply Chain Finance, Agile-Hybrid Project Management, and Islamic Sustainable Finance. Furthermore, it formulates a deterministic mathematical model linking Earned Value Management indices with automated, smart-contract-driven Islamic financing disbursements (Parallel Istisna’a and Tokenized Murabaha) verified by IoT Digital Twins. The integration of AI-driven Digital Twins and permissioned blockchain ledgers resolves the historical operational bottleneck of Islamic banking: the high

papers.title: The design and impact of a dual-agent artificial intelligence system in personalised mathematics tutoring
papers.summary: Digital tutoring tools are increasingly used in schools to support mathematics learning, but empirical evidence remains limited on how diagnostic and instructional functions can be coordinated to provide personalised support. This study examined a dual-agent intervention in which a diagnostic agent generated provisional learning-profile classifications (diverging, assimilating, converging, and accommodating) and a personalised tutoring agent delivered profile-responsive, stage-specific guidance within Polya’s (1945) problem-solving framework; a general tutoring agent provided non-profile-responsive guidance in the control condition. The quasi-experimental study involved 206 Chinese grade 5 students, including 99 in the experimental group and 107 in the control group. The pre-test and post-test used two parallel mathematics tasks evaluated using the same analytic rubric, and learning gain was calculated from these matched assessment components. The experimental group achieved a significantly larger mean gain than the control group (5.14 vs. 0.94, t(204) = 4.36, p < .001, Hedges’ g = .61). A baseline-adjusted sensitivity analysis confirmed the overall group effect (p < .001). After Holm correction for four profile-specific comparisons, only the assimilating-profile contrast remained significant (adjusted p = .0496). However, the omnibus group-by-profile interaction was not signif

papers.title: Delegating or Doing? Understanding User Behavior in Hybrid Human–Agent Interfaces
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into applications, allowing users to complete tasks either through direct manipulation or by delegating actions to conversational agents. However, little is known about how users balance these modalities when both are available. We present a web-based content management system augmented with an LLM agent through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling users to perform CRUD tasks through a graphical interface, a conversational agent, or both. We conducted a between-subjects study (N=73) comparing three interaction modes: Traditional-Only, AI-First, and Hybrid. Across sixteen scenarios, we analyzed task completion time, interaction logs, and delegation behavior. AI-assisted interaction significantly reduced clicks, page navigations, and scrolling, indicating lower interaction effort. Surprisingly, these reductions did not translate into faster task completion, as task duration did not differ significantly across conditions. We also found no significant relationship between CRUD operation type and delegation, suggesting that users did not systematically avoid delegating higher-risk actions. Instead, delegation varied far more between participants than between tasks, with individual differences accounting for roughly half the variance in assistant use (ICC =.50). Our findings suggest that the primary benefit of human–agent i

papers.title: A flexible agent-based modelling framework of multi-serotype pneumococcal carriage to evaluate vaccine strategies in large populations
papers.summary: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a multi-serotype pathogen causing a substantial global burden of pneumonia and invasive bacterial disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been implemented worldwide, protecting against colonisation and disease from selected high-burden serotypes, but in many settings short-term effectiveness has been eroded by serotype replacement. Vaccines with broader serotype coverage have been developed, at the cost of immunogenicity against single serotypes. To determine the longer-term impact of these new formulations, we propose a novel modelling framework that evaluates the relationship between serotype-specific vaccine immunogenicity and effectiveness, comprising immunity, carriage and clinical models. Dynamics of individual serotypes are modelled over time, advancing existing modelling paradigms that group all serotypes according to vaccine type. This framework is sufficiently flexible to consider diverse populations, emerging vaccine formulations and implementation strategies. A retrospective analysis of sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccines in Australia demonstrates the flexibility of the model.

papers.title: X-SYS: A Reference Architecture for Interactive Explanation Systems
papers.summary: The explainable AI (XAI) research community has proposed numerous technical methods, yet deploying explainability as systems remains challenging: Interactive explanation systems require both suitable algorithms and system capabilities that maintain explanation usability across repeated queries, evolving models and data, and governance constraints. We argue that operationalizing XAI requires treating explainability as an information systems problem where user interaction demands induce specific system requirements. We introduce X-SYS, a reference architecture for interactive explanation systems, that guides (X)AI researchers, developers and practitioners in connecting interactive explanation user interfaces (XUI) with system capabilities. X-SYS organizes around four quality attributes named STAR (scalability, traceability, responsiveness, and adaptability), and specifies a five-component decomposition (XUI Services, Explanation Services, Model Services, Data Services, Orchestration and Governance). It maps interaction patterns to system capabilities to decouple user interface evolution from backend computation. We implement X-SYS through SemanticLens, a system for semantic search and activation steering in vision-language models. papers.title: Verifying Reasoning Chains Generated by Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are extensively used for many Natural Language Processing tasks such as question answering, natural language inference, document summarization, etc. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting compels LLMs to generate step-by-step reasoning chains. While some of the reasoning chains may follow a correct thought process, they can also suffer from hallucinations, leading to errors in answer generation. Recently, many articles have targeted the problem of verifying these reasoning chains from various aspects. Despite this recent attention, to the best of our knowledge, no comprehensive survey currently summarizes these studies on reasoning chain verification. This work addresses that gap by presenting a detailed overview of the methods for verifying reasoning chains and categorizing them according to their methodology. This paper introduces a novel taxonomy of existing reasoning chain verification methods and mainly divides them into approaches that assess entire chains versus those that examine individual steps. This paper also reviews benchmarks for evaluating reasoning chains and verification methods and further discusses the challenges and future directions associated with these methods. By compiling and analyzing these approaches, our survey aims to advance the understanding and development of robust reasoning techniques in LLMs.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder: pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, animal models, and potential therapeutic strategies
papers.summary: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complex neurobehavioral disorder that disproportionately affects military service members. The clinical presentation of PTSD is heterogeneous and may overlap with other psychiatric conditions. According to the Fifth Edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5), common symptoms include memory loss, mood and personality changes, impulsiveness, aggression, anxiety, and depression. The pathophysiological mechanisms underlying PTSD remain incompletely understood, although research implicates pathways involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, dysfunctional neural circuitry, neurochemical imbalances, neuroinflammatory processes, and genetic and epigenetic factors. Approximately 7% of the U.S. adult population has met the diagnostic criteria for PTSD in their lifetime, with a substantially higher prevalence of 12%-30% among military personnel. Multiple animal models, including single-stressor, intermediate complexity, social interaction, predator stress, and blast exposure paradigms, have been employed to investigate PTSD mechanisms. Current treatment strategies typically integrate pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy. Military service members are at increased risk for blast injuries, which frequently result in traumatic brain injury (TBI). Although some symptoms of TBI may resolve, approximately 20%

papers.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
papers.summary: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. We added TDD to their pilot workflow, using a design science approach, with continuous refinements to prompt design and workflow structure, based on observed AI behavior. The generated code was evaluated and compared with non-TDD code, using SonarQube for static code analysis. The results indicate that TDD reduced complexity and code duplication, but introduced more quality issues overall, while non-TDD produced fewer, but more severe issues. The generated tests from the TDD workflow focused more on content verification than on behavioral testing, contributing to a lower code coverage per test compared to non-TDD. The findings suggest that TDD involves trade-offs that may favor certain development priorities, in particular where lower complexity and reduced duplication are more beneficial than minimizing total issue count. This indicates that a strict application of TDD may not be optimal in an autonomous AI-driven context, and that exploring more flexible adaptations of the TDD workflow remains interesting for future resea

papers.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
papers.summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, an

papers.title: CliniCIRCA: LLM-powered Clinical Timeline Generation and Summarization from Unstructured EHR Texts for Mental Health Patients
papers.summary: Abstract Background: Mental health care often requires clinicians to reason over patient journeys: longitudinal patterns of symptoms, diagnoses, treatments, behaviors, social context, and responses to care. Yet these journeys are rarely documented as readily available, explicit timelines. Clinically important temporal information is often embedded in unstructured discharge narratives, where events may be repeated, narrated out of order, or expressed through vague and relative time references. This makes temporal recovery difficult for clinicians and computational systems, and can limit the reliability of downstream summarization. Methods: We present CliniCIRCA, a multi-stage large language model (LLM) framework for Calendar-anchored, Imprecision-aware Reconstruction of Clinical Annals. CliniCIRCA decomposes patient-journey reconstruction into three stages: extracting atomic clinical events from raw discharge summaries, assigning calendar-grounded temporal labels with explicit uncertainty, and rendering the verified timeline as a date-grouped clinical summary. The framework is designed to make temporal reasoning inspectable rather than hidden inside a single summarization step. Results: From 14,882 MIMIC-III mental-health-coded admissions, we construct a benchmark of 52 discharge summaries on which CliniCIRCA produces 15,891 temporally tagged events. Following clinician-defined

papers.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals
papers.summary: Abstract Understanding human motor control requires integrating cortical and spinal activity, muscle mechanics, and electrophysiology, which are typically studied in isolation. We present MyoGen, an open-source framework that unifies spinal circuitry, proprioceptive feedback, musculotendon dynamics, and multimodal electromyography generation. Using data-driven optimization benchmarked against human motor unit recordings, MyoGen produces motor unit population activity matching experimental discharge-rate distributions and variability across muscles. The framework generates decomposable surface and intramuscular electromyography, reproduces beta-band modulation of descending drive and its transformation into force, and implements key sensorimotor loop components. Dimensionality reduction of simulated agonist-antagonist electromyography reveals low-dimensional control manifolds consistent with recordings from able-bodied individuals and those with spinal cord injury. Here, we show that MyoGen provides a physiologically grounded simulation substrate, enabling systematic investigation of motor control principles, benchmarking of signal-processing algorithms, and exploration of experimentally inaccessible sensorimotor interactions.

papers.title: Reasoning More, Knowing No Better? Epistemic Calibration in Financial Reasoning Tasks
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) reportedly ‘reason’ with increasing sophistication, but whether they ‘know’ when they are wrong remains poorly understood. We study epistemic calibration, the alignment between expressed confidence and empirical correctness, across approximately 30 contemporary models and configurable reasoning-effort budgets, using XFinBench (graduate-level financial reasoning) and SQuAD v2 (answerable and unanswerable questions). Reported confidence stays high relative to accuracy, with weak discrimination between correct and incorrect or unsupported answers. Miscalibration follows a Dunning–Kruger–like pattern: weaker models are often strongly overconfident, while frontier models are mildly underconfident. Reasoning effort significantly improves accuracy but has no detectable effect on the confidence–accuracy gap or ECE; stable between-model differences explain over 96% of calibration variance, versus a negligible effort effect. Calibration deteriorates most on scenario planning and numerical modeling. On SQuAD v2, models answer four in five unanswerable questions and remain near-maximally confident even when no answer is supported; higher reasoning effort yields no robust gain in calibration or abstention after multiplicity correction. We discuss implications for evaluation, deployment, and the design of calibration-aware, boundary-aware financial reasoning syst

papers.title: Machine thinking and the human mind
papers.summary: Abstract This opinion article examines the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence by contrasting human intelligence with machine capabilities across physical, perceptual, cognitive, metacognitive, and social dimensions. As AI shifts from narrow task‐oriented models to general‐purpose agents and autonomous systems, the article addresses critical technical and existential challenges, including model hallucinations, opaque capabilities, and skills displacement. To ensure AI is safe and beneficial alignment with human interests, it advocates moving beyond conventional post‐training techniques toward objective‐driven architectures grounded in self‐awareness, metacognition, and human values. Ultimately, the piece calls for reorienting education and society to cultivate the human mind—fostering ethical, compassionate polymaths capable of thriving alongside advanced machine intelligence.

papers.title: Advancing Learner Autonomy in Adult Online Education: An Evidence-Based Framework for Practice
papers.summary: Online learning in higher education continues to expand, but persistent challenges of student isolation, disconnection, and retention require innovative engagement strategies. Self-regulation and autonomy play a critical role, and the ability to develop skills in planning, managing, and controlling their learning behaviors is critical to student success. Engagement is widely recognized as essential for learner satisfaction and course completion, and research consistently indicates a clear link between instructor engagement, learner engagement, and actual learning. Successful on-ground instruction does not always translate to successful online instruction, and facilitators require appropriate professional development related to online delivery and methodologies. Ensuring online learner success requires a combination of intentional course design, proactive support, and the cultivation of learner self-regulation skills. To facilitate persistence and understand and effectively address the multiple needs of a diverse adult learner population, instructors must implement andragogical strategies that will keep learners motivated and actively engaged. Heutagogy is of particular interest to adult online education, which shares key attributes with it, such as learner autonomy and self-direction, and has roots in adult teaching and learning. papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: An Assessment of Accessibility and Affordability of Inpatient Psychiatric Care in Tennessee
papers.summary: Introduction: Access to mental health has seen changes over the past decade, but little research and attention have been given to access to inpatient psychiatric facilities. Inpatient psychiatric care is crucial for patients experiencing mental health emergencies who need immediate access to care. Gaps in spatial accessibility, affordability, and the access and assessment process were identified due to a lack of available information in the field. Methods: Secondary data from the Tennessee Department of Health were used to assess financial accessibility through payer source charges and patient encounters, as well as through mapping of inpatient psychiatric facilities and conducting drive time and coverage area analyses. Primary data were collected through interviews with clinicians located in Northeastern Tennessee to gain insight into the assessment process and gather their perceptions of inpatient care. Results: Longitudinal descriptive reviews on the financial accessibility among Tennessee Inpatient Facilities. This showed increased variability among facilities when stratified by region, ownership, and type of operation. Spatial accessibility in ArcGIS showed 82% of counties were not covered within a 30-minute radius of inpatient facilities. Analysis showed that Middle Tennessee had significantly less coverage from inpatient facilities and raised concerns about spatial-socia

papers.title: Pieces Solving a Puzzle: Emerging Roles and Cross-Field Analogies During a Distributed Epistemic Game
papers.summary: In an effort to describe why some problems can’t be solved, a character compared them to a cubic meter of platinum - a block so dense that all the people who could squeeze around it still couldn’t lift it off the ground. In the same way, these problems simply can’t have enough people gathered around and communicating about them - and so they remain unsolved. This research looks at the first Polymath Project (2009) as an example of a distributed epistemic game to examine how groups engage with complex problems. and without a locally omniscient individual. In this setting of epistemic uncertainty, interactions between individuals reveal patterns of participation, and an analogy opens a new solution pathway by introducing a problem-solving approach from another field. These insights answer the initial question of the Polymath Project - ‘Is massively collaborative mathematics possible?’ - and offer hope for lifting the cubic meter of other unsolvable problems.

papers.title: Sex-Dependent Modulation of the Endocannabinoid System in Pain Processing
papers.summary: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. This would suggest that hormones have a different effect on males and females, leading to differences in the cannabinoid’s pain-relieving ability. Lastly, I sough

papers.title: Phenotypic discovery of GABAA receptor-mediated general anesthetics with analgesic activity
papers.summary: Abstract General anesthetics are essential for invasive medical procedures; however, there remains a need for safer agents. Using a bespoke 96-well-plate format platform enabling high-throughput imaging of larval zebrafish behavior, we screen 12,000 compounds and identify an isoxazole chemotype that phenocopies the intravenous anesthetics etomidate and propofol. Its optimization via medicinal chemistry yields an anesthetic that we call nidradine. This anesthetic is efficacious in both zebrafish and mice and lacks the problematic adrenal suppression characteristic of etomidate. Mechanistic studies using electrophysiology and structural biology reveal that nidradine, like etomidate and propofol, is a positive allosteric modulator of the GABA A receptor. Remarkably, behavioral assays in mice demonstrate that nidradine differs from most general anesthetics in that it also produces analgesia at subsedative doses.

papers.title: Actualizing the external enablement of generative artificial intelligence: evidence from software new ventures
papers.summary: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools have been argued to enable entrepreneurial endeavors. Employing the external enablement framework, we examine how, if at all, the venture-level benefits offered by GenAI tools – termed GenAI enablement – are actualized in new ventures. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative design with 10 entrepreneurs in the software industry and five AI-entrepreneurship experts, we capture instances where entrepreneurs succeed or fail to capitalize on GenAI enablement and analyze the mechanisms underlying these different pathways. Findings Our findings lead to a model that outlines the actualization pathways of GenAI enablement, emphasizing that the properties of enablement (i.e. opacity, agency-intensity and outcome-variability) – beyond the mere availability of GenAI enablement – are crucial in explaining whether and how enablement is actualized. Research limitations/implications Given the small sample and specific research context during the early diffusion of GenAI, our findings warrant further examination across industries, countries and stages of technological diffusion. Future research could test and extend our model by examining the roles of outcome-variability and insufficient enablement in determining whether and how GenAI enablement is actualized, as well as how its actualization relates to venture performance. papers.title: Feedback Actionability in AI-Mediated L2 Interaction: A Repeated-Session Study of Learner Uptake
papers.summary: AI systems can respond to nearly every learner turn, but how learners use that feedback during an exchange is less well documented. This study followed 48 university EFL learners across eight text-based classroom sessions using GPT-4o (384 learner-session observations), examining participation, words per turn (WPT), and researcher-coded next-turn uptake. Following each session, learners submitted ChatGPT-generated summaries of their messages, while researchers separately coded immediate revisions from the interaction records. Mean learner turns increased from 12.3 to 14.5, WPT from 29.3 to 34.6, and mean learner-session uptake from 0.36 to 0.68. Mixed-effects models showed positive session associations with WPT (B = 0.663, p < .001) and uptake (logit B = 0.181, p < .001). After accounting for the session trend, a supplementary model did not identify a distinct phase-level uptake difference following the midpoint prompt revision (B = 0.153, p = .327). The study documents increasing immediate use of AI feedback during repeated interaction, although the fixed phase order prevents separating prompt refinement from accumulated classroom experience.

papers.title: Emotionally Aware AI Chatbots for Adolescents: A Review of Psychological Principles for Learning, Calibrated Trust, and Healthy Human–AI Interaction
papers.summary: Conversational artificial intelligence now belongs to ordinary adolescent life, but the psychological research that should guide its design spreads over fields which seldom cite each other. Research on adolescent development, on misinformation susceptibility, on trust in automation, on chatbot-supported learning and on companion-chatbot overreliance has grown up separately, and each of these areas answers only part of the question of how a general-purpose chatbot should talk to a teenager. This paper brings together twenty-one sources from developmental psychology, human factors, human-computer interaction and educational technology, in order to show what is now known about adolescent chatbot interaction and what this means for conversational design. Three results appear repeatedly in this research. First, adolescence is a design context of its own, not a smaller version of adulthood, since reward sensitivity, social influence and emotional regulation are still developing, while exposure to persuasive conversational systems has already reached almost everyone. Second, trust in a chatbot changes behavior in ways that can be measured; thus, the proper design target is calibrated trust rather than maximal trust.
